newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South Africa bonds gained more than ten basis points on Tuesday, inspired by sharp gains in U.S. Treasuries after the release of benign U.S. consumer price inflation numbers.
The data -- which provided the main impetus for the day on the local market -- showed U.S. consumer prices rose 0.1 percent in March against an expected 0.2 percent.
The core U.S. rate, stripped of the volatile energy and food categories, rose 0.2 percent against a forecast 0.3 percent.
After the data came in below expectations, the U.S. T-bond fell one full point, but ticked up again to last trade at 7.10 percent from 7.18 percent earlier.
"The numbers were good...it certainly looks as if activity in the U.S. is slowing down enough not to necessitate further (U.S.) interest rate hikes," a dealer at a leading bank said.
He said the local market had taken inspiration from the eagerly awaited figures, with the benchmark R150 bond firming more than ten basis points from its previous closing levels.
At 1620 GMT the R150 stock was at 15.20 percent from 15.31 percent late on Monday.
Despite the day's gains, bond traders said the market was hampered by a lack of direction, taking its cue from any external factors.
"Today's moves were purely on the back of the U.S. and we have not seen any large institutional flows," one commented.
He expected a sideways drift on Wednesday in the absence of fresh news, predicting a range around 15.15 to 15.30 percent.
No domestic economic data is due out, although in the U.S., March industrial production data is expected at 1315 GMT.
Foreigners were net buyers of 288.24 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Monday after buying 171.67 million on Friday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 3.34 billion rand on Monday from 607.96 million rand on Friday.
On the forex market, the rand posted late gains as offshore players sold dollars soon after the release of the better-than-expected CPI numbers.
"Most of the dollar selling came out of London and it was bond-related rand trading," one forex trader said.
At 1420 GMT the rand was at 4.4590/4620 against a strong dollar from 4.4555/4585 overnight and a best intraday bid of 4.4575.
Traders expected a weaker trend on Wednesday, particularly as the dollar remained strong against most international currencies.
It rose to a fresh 37-month peak of 1.7375 marks in early York trade on Tuesday, before retracing to be last quoted at around 1.7320.
"We should go weaker tomorrow on the strong dollar with 4.48 a big levels to break on the topside," a second dealer said.
Against the crosses, the rand was last trading at 28.3137/3552 yen from 28.3279/3694 yen, 0.3885/3889 marks from 0.3863/3868 marks and 7.2467/2547 rand against sterling from 7.2282/2353 rand.
On the money market, three-month deposit rates were quoted steady in a 16.60 to 16.65 percent offered range, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at between 15.95 and 16.10 percent.
South Africa's money market shortage rose back above the nine billion rand mark to 9.283 billion rand on Monday from 8.175 billion rand on Saturday, the Reserve Bank said.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
